heroLead: West Brownsville sits on the Monongahela River across from Brownsville, in a stretch of Washington County that carried both old coal history and new gas leasing.
intro: There's a particular kind of tired that comes from a small river town like West Brownsville where the coal money left generations ago and the gas money showed up promising something similar, then got complicated fast. We've sat at kitchen tables in towns just like it.

A lot of the mineral ownership along this stretch of the Monongahela traces back to farms and river-bottom parcels that got broken into pieces long before anyone drilled a Marcellus well. If you're holding one of those pieces and wondering what it's actually worth today, we'll tell you plainly.

sections.heading: River-Bottom Ownership Is Rarely Simple
paragraphs: West Brownsville's mineral estates were frequently severed from the surface a century ago, often tied to old coal leases before gas was ever the target. That history means the mineral estate and the surface estate can belong to entirely different people today, and the paperwork tying them together is not always clean.

When we evaluate a West Brownsville interest, we're checking whether your mineral rights were carried forward correctly through every sale and every generation, because a break anywhere in that chain affects what a buyer can safely pay.

sections.heading: What Act 13 Impact Fees Do and Don't Cover You For
paragraphs: Pennsylvania's Act 13 impact fee sends money to counties and municipalities with unconventional wells, Washington County included, to offset road wear, emergency services, and local infrastructure. It's a real fee operators pay, but it has nothing to do with what lands in your royalty check.
We mention it because owners sometimes assume Act 13 money is somehow flowing back to them personally. It isn't. Your royalty is governed entirely by your lease, and that's the document we focus on.

sections.heading: Selling Versus Holding a Small Interest
paragraphs: Small or fractional interests near West Brownsville often get treated as afterthoughts by operators, showing up on statements as tiny, irregular payments that barely cover the cost of tracking them. For some families, converting that into one clean payment now makes more sense than decades of small, unpredictable checks.
We're not going to tell you selling is right for everyone. We'll tell you what your specific interest is worth to us and let you weigh that against what you're actually receiving now.

faqs.question: Does West Brownsville have active Marcellus production nearby?
faqs.answer: Washington County overall has significant Marcellus activity, and specific production near your parcel depends on the unit it's pooled into. We check that as part of our review.

faqs.question: My family's mineral rights were severed from a coal deed decades ago. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Severed estates are common in this part of Pennsylvania. We trace the chain of title through the Washington County recorder of deeds to confirm ownership.

faqs.question: How fast can a sale close?
faqs.answer: Once title is confirmed clean, most of our deals close in a matter of weeks, not months.
